items.title: 68357_Jimmy Maxwell oral history interview
items.q: [INTERVIEWER] I know the great black jazz poet, John Hendricks...

ctx.x: Some of the creations were so great.

So very descriptive. I know the great black jazz poet, John Hendricks, he has some tremendous expressions like that. He compares a West Indian black and a Caribbean black to an American black in a song which he sings, 'If you have a ship and you needed some rum, then you would stop at the Islands. So some stopped on the way to trade some slaves for some rum,' and he says, some stopped on the way, and the rest came on to the U.S.A. So some of the West Indians, some of the Caribbean slaves, were sold for rum, and…
could, so they say 'dis for this, and dat for that. And he says, it was pretty good for that saying.
